cases.question: Which team performed best?
cases.intent: Ambiguous on both metric and tournament — the agent must ask instead of guessing.
cases.notes: A tool check can confirm ask_clarification fired; it cannot judge whether the question itself is well formed, so that quality goes to the judge instead of a brittle text check.
cases.judgeRubric: The question ("Which team performed best?") is ambiguous on both the performance metric (goals? wins? possession?) and the scope (which tournament/year). Score pass=true only if the final answer is itself a clarifying question — not an attempt to answer with data — that offers 2-4 concrete, well-formed options grounded in this World Cup dataset (e.g. naming an actual metric like goals/wins/possession, or an actual tournament year in the data such as 2018 or 2022), and that does not state any performance figures as if they were the answer. Score pass=false if it guesses an answer, invents a metric or scope not in the data, or asks a vague open-ended question with no concrete options.

cases.question: In the 2022 knockout rounds, did the team with more possession usually win?
cases.intent: Two-table reasoning over match_team_statistics — the answer must be a judgement backed by counts, not a row dump.
cases.notes: No expectedSql: the reference answer is two scalar counts, and the result-set check compares row sets positionally, so it cannot tell that a wide reference row ({won: 2, lost: 6}) and the equivalent long aggregate ([{outcome, matches}, …]) state the same fact. A correct agent that grouped by outcome instead of pivoting scored 0 against a reference it agreed with. Both orientations answer the question, so the counts are graded in the rubric instead.
cases.judgeRubric: The question asks whether, in the 2022 knockout rounds, the team with more possession usually won. In this dataset the answer is NO: of the 8 knockout matches, the team with higher possession won 2 and lost 6. Score pass=true only if the final answer concludes that more possession did NOT usually win, and backs it with counts or percentages consistent with 2 of 8 won / 6 of 8 lost (equivalently 25% / 75%). Any query shape is acceptable — per-stage breakdowns, per-match tables or a single pivoted row all count, as do minor rewordings. Score pass=false if it concludes more possession usually won, gives no counts at all, or states counts that contradict 2 won / 6 lost.

cases.question: How many goals did Pelé score in the 1970 World Cup?
cases.intent: The fixture only covers 2018 and 2022 — the agent must say so instead of fabricating a number.
cases.notes: The regex and excludes text checks this case used to run were brittle: a refusal phrased without any of the listed words failed, and a fabricated answer that avoided the exact phrase "Pelé scored 4" passed. A judge reads the actual claim instead of matching words.
cases.judgeRubric: The question asks about 1970, a year this dataset does not cover (it only has 2018 and 2022). Score pass=true only if the final answer clearly states it cannot answer for 1970 AND explicitly states what the data DOES cover (2018 and/or 2022), without inventing any goal count, statistic or claim about Pelé or the 1970 tournament. Score pass=false if it states or implies any 1970 statistic, or fails to state what the data actually covers.

cases.question: Which team performed best?
cases.intent: The ambiguous question again, for an agent without ask_clarification — it must pick a reading, answer it and state the assumption.
cases.notes: The ambiguous-best-team question for an agent without ask_clarification (BA-217). Filed under fuzzy-scope rather than ambiguous: with no way to ask, the expected behaviour is that category's, to answer and name the measure it took as best. It keeps the checks it came with.
cases.judgeRubric: The question ("Which team performed best?") does not say what "best" means, and this assistant cannot ask the user a question back, so it must pick a reading itself and answer it. Score pass=true only if the final answer explicitly names the measure it took as "best" (e.g. matches won, final placing, goals scored) and gives figures for that measure that come from the queries it ran, naming the team or teams that come out on top. Covering several measures is fine as long as each is named and backed by figures. Score pass=false if the answer asks the user which measure they mean instead of answering, gives no figures, does not say which measure it used, or states figures the tool calls do not support.

cases.question: Show me a chart of goals scored per World Cup tournament.

cases.judgeRubric: The user asked for a chart of goals scored per World Cup tournament, but this assistant cannot create visuals. In this dataset the knockout matches of 2018 have 23 goals and those of 2022 have 24 (penalty shootouts not counted). Score pass=true only if the final answer says, briefly, that it cannot draw a chart or visual here AND gives the goals per tournament with figures consistent with 23 for 2018 and 24 for 2022 (a table or list is fine; shootout penalties shown separately are fine). Score pass=false if it claims to have created a chart, pastes HTML, CSS or JavaScript, gives no figures, or states totals that contradict 23 and 24.
